newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Reynolds sees stable earnings.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Reynolds sees stable earnings.

text.p: Reynolds Philippine Corp, the country's dominant aluminum manufacturer, is expected to show stable growth in earnings because of its exposure to different sectors in a growing economy, company officials and the manager of its share float said on Monday.

Reynolds will start offering on February 5 some 238 million shares to the public at 4.55 pesos each, that would raise about 1.1 billion pesos. The public will own 34 percent of the firm's expanded capital after the offering.

"With the products of the company not only serving the consumer sectors but also the industrial, property, power and telecommunication sectors...Reynolds' product diversity will enable it not only to take advantage of the growth of the different sectors but also reduces the risk and improves the stability of income and revenue sources," Wilfred Racadio, vice president of float manager All Asia Capital and Trust Co, said at a news conference.

The company has projected a net income of 301 million pesos this year, 56 percent higher than last year's estimate of 193 million pesos. In 1995, its net profit was 107 million pesos, according to Jorge Navarra, the firm's chief financial officer.
The earnings include contributions from subsidiaries of a projected 160 million pesos in 1997 from an estimated 119 million pesos in 1996, the company said.

Reynolds owns 60 percent of Fuji Reynolds Fabrication Corp, an aluminum fabrication and installation company; and 49 percent of Leader ReyPhil Corp, a joint venture with the Hong Kong unit of Malaysia's Leader Universal Holdings Berhad.
Universal is involved in the manufacture of aluminum and copper wire rods, transmission cables and copper telecom cables.
Reynolds also expects to get earnings from its 100 percent stake in New Saga Power Corp, which has a 39.5 percent stake in a 110 mw power plant in Batangas, south of Manila.

Reynolds' offer price of 4.55 pesos is equivalent to 10.6 times the forecast 1997 earnings per share of 37 centavos, which is at a 40 percent discount to the local stock market and a 61 percent discount to six comparable listed Asian aluminum companies, All Asia said.
Jaime Gonzales, the firm's president, said the proceeds of the float will mostly go to the retirement of debt and only 67 million pesos will be set aside for capital spending.

He added Reynolds' public offer will yield immediate returns to new investors since the company had already met most of its capacity build-up. The company's rated capacity will be increased to 20,250 tonnes this year from only 12,800 tonnes in 1995.
